title: Seahorse Close-Up — 10 Things to Notice

facts.title: Upright swimmer
facts.text: A seahorse usually swims with its body upright, rather than in the horizontal posture typical of many fishes.

facts.title: Bony armor
facts.text: Bony plates support and protect its body beneath the skin; rings continue along its flexible tail.

facts.title: Frequent meals
facts.text: Big-bellied seahorses lack a true stomach for storing food, so they need to feed frequently.

facts.title: Small fins
facts.text: The dorsal fin and paired pectoral fins help with movement and control. A much smaller anal fin is also present.

facts.title: A grasping tail
facts.text: The prehensile tail can wrap around vegetation and other supports to help the animal hold position.

facts.title: An ambush hunter
facts.text: Big-bellied seahorses often wait among vegetation for small crustaceans to come within reach.

facts.title: Suction feeding
facts.text: A tubular snout directs suction that draws small prey into the mouth.

facts.title: Independent eyes
facts.text: The eyes can move independently, helping a seahorse watch its surroundings.

facts.title: No chewing
facts.text: Seahorses have no teeth; prey small enough to enter the mouth is swallowed whole.

facts.title: A male brood pouch
facts.text: The female transfers eggs into the male’s pouch. He broods the developing young and later gives birth.
